blocks.text: How Russian words are built: a prefix, a root, suffixes, an ending.

== Word formation ==

Russian has on hand a set of prefixes, prepositional and adverbial in nature, as well as diminutive, augmentative, and frequentative suffixes. All of these can be stacked one upon the other to produce multiple derivatives of a given word. Participles and other inflectional forms may also have a special connotation.

One prefix can carry several meanings: у- in уйти́ means “away”, but not in every word that starts with у-. So this course groups prefixes and suffixes by meaning, and puts a word under a meaning only where a dictionary lists it there: the Russian Wiktionary's numbered meanings of each prefix and suffix with their examples, the English Wiktionary's, and the English Wikipedia's table of prefixed verbs of motion. Roots come last, as the families the Russian Wiktionary lists, one family per meaning where a root has two. The practice uses real sentences from Tatoeba with their English.
